title: Private upgrade operator for data-plane zero-impact switchover
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a Kubernetes-native upgrade operator and Terraform IaC modules to perform rolling upgrades of the private data-plane/runtime with zero customer impact and automated safe rollback triggers. The operator must coordinate canary pods, KV cache warmup, connection draining, health gate checks, and traffic switchover via the customer's LB/Envoy. This ticket scopes the operator design, Terraform module spec, health probes contract, and automated rollback policies for VPC/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can perform a canary upgrade (single pod) and promote to fleet with traffic shift without 99th-percentile latency increase > 10% or error rate increase > 0.5% over baseline
Automated rollback triggers on sustained SLO breach (5m error rate >0.5% or p95 latency regression >15%) and restores previous runtime version within SLA window
Terraform module provisions operator CRDs, ServiceAccount + IAM roles, network ACLs, and can be run idempotently (plan/app) in customer VPC templates
Health probe contract documented and validated: /internal/health (liveness), /internal/ready (readiness with KV cache status), /internal/accept (post-warm acceptance tests)
End-to-end e2e test harness executes synthetic traffic scenarios and verifies canary cold-start, cache-warm, and rollback path in CI
implementation_notes: Operator design: state machine with phases: PRECHECK -> CANARY -> VALIDATE -> ROLLING -> FINISH. Each phase has timeout and retry budget.
Canary strategy: start 1 replica with traffic sampled (1-2%) using Envoy weighted routing or service mesh header. Use request shadowing for acceptance tests.
KV cache migration: prefer in-place KV warming using background prefill jobs; avoid flushing unless safe. Add cache version header to detect stale entries.
Traffic shift: use gradual weight shifts with safety gates (metric checks every 30s). Implement circuit-breaker that aborts and triggers rollback if thresholds crossed.
Rollback: three-step rollback that stops new deployments, shifts traffic back to previous version with priority weighting, drains new pods, and optionally triggers automated incident ticket.
Terraform modules: module should expose variables for image tags, canary percentage, metric thresholds, probe paths, IAM role ARNs, and enable/disable flags for auto-rollback.
Observability: emit rollout events (start, canary_success, canary_fail, rollback_initiated) to logs and structured telemetry. Add Prometheus metrics and tracing spans for rollout latency.
Security: operator must run with least privilege; ensure CSR approvals and KMS key usage for any secrets. Mark security_review_required=true.
steps: 1) Draft operator CRD schema and state machine transitions (2d design)
2) Implement Terraform module skeleton and example overlay for customer VPC (3d)
3) Implement canary controller + traffic shifting hooks (5d)
4) Add health probe contract and implement acceptance test jobs (3d)
5) Integrate observability and create Prometheus exporters and tracing (3d)
6) Build CI e2e harness with synthetic traffic and failure injection (4d)
7) Run staged rollout in internal private cluster, iterate on thresholds and timeouts (3d)
8) Prepare runbook and customer-facing docs, add feature flag gating (2d)
risks: Incorrect health probe or acceptance tests may cause false positives and unnecessary rollbacks in customer environments
IaC idempotency failures could leave operator in inconsistent state across runs
Cache warming may not be fast enough for high-QPS customers, causing initial latency spikes
Network constraints in customer VPCs (NAT timeouts, LB connector limits) could impact traffic shifting
Rollback may expose data-plane incompatibilities (protocol changes) if previous runtime is incompatible with migrated state
